leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eight members prefer optical lattice clocks in their round-1 configuration, all with the same two laureates (Katori and Ye) and citations that stress the magic-wavelength lattice and fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. Johansson and Pearce moved to B001 from second and fifth place respectively after reading the opening ballots, and Olsson ranked B013 first in the opening. What is shared: a two-name credit, independent reproduction in several laboratories, and agreement that the redefinition of the second should not be a precondition. What is not shared: how much weight the 2005 (frequency combs) and 2012 (single-quantum-system control) prizes should carry, and how to treat other early lattice-clock groups (Lemonde, Ido, Takamoto, PTB, NIST, Paris) outside the two names. Several supporters (Olsson, Danielsson, Johansson) hold B013 or B024 as a live alternative, and Lindroth would support B013 as a second choice.

Two members prefer magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, both with Bistritzer, MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero and citations built on the flat-band prediction and the correlated-insulator and superconducting states, not on a pairing mechanism. They share the theory-plus-experiment framing and the view that the core phenomena are reproduced by many groups. Both name Eva Andrei's earlier STM evidence as an unresolved attribution cost of the three-person limit, and both keep B001 as an alternative (Mehlig explicitly as the safer pick if maturity is weighted over novelty). Eriksson also keeps B004 as an alternative. B013 was ranked first by three members at opening (Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson), but Olsson now prefers B001; Pearce had ranked it second and in the opening proposed a trio with Andrei in place of Bistritzer.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members rank B001 and every member who addresses it accepts the Katori-Ye pairing as a clean two-person credit; no member rejects the clocks on scientific grounds, and the disagreement is about relative ranking and distinctness from earlier prizes.

No member makes the prize conditional on the formal redefinition of the second; Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Pearce and Olsson treat the demonstrated and reproduced 1e-18 accuracy as the discovery, with the redefinition as a later consequence.

Members on both sides state that the superconducting pairing mechanism in twisted bilayer graphene is open and that any B013 citation should rest on flat bands and the correlated and superconducting phases, not on a settled microscopic explanation.

Topological insulators (B024) are described as scientifically important and mature or arguably overdue by Pearce, Danielsson, Kroll, Olsson and Mehlig, even though no member prefers them in round 1, and they are an alternative for six members.

Circuit QED (B029) is acknowledged as a real invention, but Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Johansson (who declared proximity and discounted his own ranking) all place it below the leading candidates this round, mainly because of the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits.
scientific_disputes: Whether the lattice clock is a distinct discovery or an incremental step in optical frequency metrology after the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 single-ion-control prizes. Supporters (Pearce, Kroll, Johansson, Danielsson, Olsson) argue that state-insensitive trapping of many neutral atoms at a magic wavelength is new; Eriksson and Mehlig regard the conceptual step beyond precision metrology as smaller than for a new platform of correlated matter and rank B013 first for that reason.

Whether the twisted bilayer graphene result is secure enough to honour now: Eriksson and Mehlig regard the prediction, correlated insulators and superconducting domes as robust and reproduced across platforms, while Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce stress the open pairing mechanism, twist-angle disorder and uneven device-level reproducibility.

Whether the overlap of B013 with the 2010 graphene prize and the 2016 topological-phases prize, raised by Eriksson, should be counted against it, and whether the overlap of B001 with 2005 and 2012 should be counted against it to the same degree.
Whether B024 and B004 are one topological-insulator prize with different credit splits or two distinct proposals, which Mehlig and Pearce note changes the competition with B013 and B001.
attribution_disputes: B001: the credit is two names, but Lemonde, Ido, Takamoto and the PTB, NIST and Paris groups are cited by Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Pearce and Olsson as early contributors outside Katori and Ye; Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson say they have not independently verified the chronology.

B013: Eva Andrei's early STM evidence is named by Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson, Johansson, Lindroth, Danielsson and Pearce as a real claim. Eriksson and Mehlig keep Bistritzer, MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero and want Andrei's exclusion stated openly; Pearce proposed MacDonald, Andrei and Jarillo-Herrero in his opening ballot. Bistritzer and MacDonald as co-authors of the continuum model is the main argument against dropping Bistritzer.

B024 and B004: any three-name cut is contested. Danielsson proposed Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan; Pearce, Johansson, Kroll and Lindroth proposed Kane, Mele and Molenkamp; B004 substitutes Xue for Mele. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (HgTe prediction) and Hasan's three-dimensional work lie outside several trios, and Mehlig, Lindroth, Olsson and Johansson all cite this as the reason B024 ranks lower.
B029: Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf omit Girvin, Devoret, Nakamura and the transmon authors according to Danielsson and Lindroth, so its credit is also sensitive.
maturity_disputes: B013 is about eight years from the 2018 experiments; Eriksson and Mehlig regard the 2011 prediction and the subsequent reproduction as a long enough chain, while Johansson, Danielsson, Kroll and Pearce see the field as moving fast with the superconductivity unresolved.

B001 is described as mature by its supporters, but Lindroth, Pearce and Olsson record that the redefinition of the second has not happened and some societal payoff is prospective; Mehlig says that if the committee weighs maturity over novelty B001 is the safer choice, while Eriksson weights conceptual break more heavily.
B024 is mature and long-confirmed, so the dispute there is about credit scope and not about timing.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (Chalmers, WACQT director): B029 falls within his own research and he states he should recuse himself from any decision on B029; he has discounted it in his round-1 preference. He reports no conflict for B001, B013 or B024.

Kroll: a research stay in John Hall's laboratory during his doctoral period; Hall is not a candidate but his 2005 prize is the closest prior-prize lineage to B001, so this could bear on how Kroll weighs distinctness. Kroll also notes that his Lund atomic-physics and quantum-memory work is adjacent to B041 and B046.
Eriksson: he uses dynamical mean-field theory and would consider recusal if B008 were seriously considered; he also notes that precision metrology is outside his expertise.
Lindroth: atomic theory is close to clock physics, disclosed as a possible bias but not a recusal issue; no tie to Katori or Ye.

Olsson: Chalmers colleague of Johansson, who ranks B029 first, disclosed as collegial and not specific to B001. Pearce (chair): no conflict for B001, B013 or B024; familiarity with astroparticle instrumentation would be flagged if a neutrino-telescope candidate were considered.
questions_for_round2: For B001: what exactly is new relative to the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 prize for single-ion control, and can a citation state that (many neutral atoms at a magic wavelength reaching the 1e-18 level) without implying credit to other clock groups?

For B001: do members who prefer it accept that Lemonde, Ido, Takamoto and the PTB, NIST and Paris groups can be left outside a Katori-Ye prize, and can any member who has checked the priority chronology report it, since Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson relied on general knowledge?

For B013: does the committee accept Bistritzer, MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero with Andrei's exclusion stated openly, or is a Pearce-style substitution of Andrei for Bistritzer defensible, and would the prize be acceptable to the five B001 supporters who cite Andrei if that question were settled?

For B013: can a citation resting only on the flat-band prediction and the correlated and superconducting phases satisfy the maturity concern, given that the pairing mechanism is open, and would Johansson, Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce treat that as sufficient?

For B001 versus B013: should the committee weigh maturity and clean attribution above conceptual novelty, and is a precision-metrology prize acceptable as the third in about twenty-five years after 2005 and 2012?

For B024 and B004: can the committee settle on a three-name allocation among Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Hasan and Xue, and take account of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, before any topological prize is treated as a serious alternative?
Can Eriksson and Mehlig say whether they would move to B001 if the Andrei and maturity questions on B013 are not resolved in round 2, and can Olsson say what would bring B013 back to first place?
summary.chair_observation: In round 1 six members prefer B001 with an identical Katori-Ye credit and two prefer B013 with an identical Bistritzer-MacDonald-Jarillo-Herrero credit; no other ballot is preferred by any member. The remaining differences are about distinctness from earlier prizes, the maturity of moire materials, and the treatment of Andrei, and I count only positions explicit in the eight files. My own movement from B024 first and B001 fifth in the opening to B001 in this round is recorded in my statement, and the shortlist alternatives B024, B004 and B029 are carried by no member as a preference.
